assertion_review.fails_if: Initial direct delivery fails or the conflicting delivery incorrectly succeeds.
Conflict handling does not actually promote the run or does not record a merge conflict.
The real repair merge does not conflict on the intended source file.
Conflict handling fails to retain a marked pointer, pending record or live worktree before finishing.
The expected repaired revision is not an ancestor of the bare remote main; the expected SHA comes from the real repair commit, while actual ancestry is read independently from Git.
The remote file lacks the combined function content; the literal expected marker is checked in remote Git content independently of the reported head.
Finishing reports a non-finished outcome or selects a head other than the actual repaired commit; the input to finish is only the run id, so these are not assertions against an echoed head argument.
Marked-pointer retirement is skipped; negative.log demonstrates exactly this failure after successful remote checks.
The held worktree directory survives successful retirement.
Git retains the worktree registration even if the directory was removed.
The successful landing retains its pending record.
The real rejecting remote hook is ignored or its refusal is not surfaced in the returned error.
The bare remote moves despite push refusal; remote_before is an independently captured pre-call Git revision.
A refused push deletes or unmarks the live pointer, removes the worktree, or removes its pending record.
The interruption stub is not reached or completion incorrectly reports success after the injected interruption.
The interruption occurs without a durable promotion row naming the actual authored commit.
The interruption fixture does not leave the pointer absent and the pending record present, so it is not testing the specified recovery state.
Finishing with an absent pointer returns a non-finished outcome; the shared remote assertions also require actual landing.
The recovery unexpectedly recreates a pointer or fails to clear the pending record.
